Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{6},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{5\pi }{12}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the top side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the top side.

For the top side, we have $v=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ and $0\le u\le \sqrt{6}.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12})),\,0\le u\le \sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a parametric equation of the line segment that makes an angle of $\frac{5\pi }{12}$ with the positive $x$-axis, where one endpoint is the point $O,$ while the other endpoint lies on the circle of radius $\sqrt{6}$ centered at $O,$ as shown below.
